learning_outcomes.text: Understands the relationship between processing and the final structure obtained from materials, and its influence on mechanical properties and in-service behavior.
Knows the most suitable processing technologies for different materials and the levels of waste generation associated with each of them.
Knows the different deterioration mechanisms of materials in service and in-service inspection techniques.
Knows the basic methods of Surface Engineering and the latest trends of interest for Mechanical Engineering.
Can select the most appropriate processing method to obtain the necessary material for a given application.
Can analyze the complete life cycle of a material when defining how to process it for a specific application.
Can select the most suitable in-service inspection technique for a problem.
Can select the most suitable surface modification technique to achieve specific properties on a surface.

syllabus_topics: 1. Metal forming processes: solidification and molding, plastic deformation, powder metallurgy.
3. Forming processes for polymer matrix composites.
4. Forming processes for ceramics and glass: traditional ceramics, advanced ceramics, glass.
5. Fusion joining technologies: metallurgy of metal welding.
7. In-service behavior: oxidation and corrosion of metals.
8. In-service behavior: brittle fracture of ceramics, creep, fatigue-creep interaction.
9. In-service failure analysis: non-destructive testing, methodology.
teaching_methods: Problem-solving and exercise classes in split groups

assessment_methods.method: Problems proposed and submitted throughout the course

assessment_rules: The progressive evaluation includes Laboratory practicals (20%), poster (10%), submitted problems (5%), partial exam (15%), and a global exam (50%). The global exam requires a minimum of 25% in each part (basic content, test, theoretical/practical questions), except 50% on basic content. If a minimum of 40% is not reached in the poster, problems, or partial exam blocks, the global exam's weight increases by the corresponding block's percentage. Alternatively, students can choose global evaluation with a global exam (80%) and a practical exam (20%). In both evaluation types, a minimum score of 40% of the maximum is required in any block to be averaged. Students must demonstrate authorship of all evaluable work in an oral interview; otherwise, the score for those activities will be zero.
